  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],

  "anova_plan": [
    "For continuous outcomes (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD): conduct one-way ANOVAs with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level factor, checking homogeneity of variance (Levene's test) and normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk or Q-Q plots)",
    "For binary Success: use chi-squared test of independence or logistic regression framework; avoid standard ANOVA due to binary response violating normality and variance assumptions",
    "If variance homogeneity violated: use Welch's ANOVA or Brown-Forsythe test for continuous variables",
    "If normality violated: consider Kruskal-Wallis tests with Dunn's post-hoc as robustness check",
    "Report effect sizes (eta-squared or partial omega-squared) for ANOVAs, odds ratios for Success analysis"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "Pairwise comparisons across all 10 possible pairs of 5 stimulation paradigms using Tukey's HSD for ANOVAs (if equal variances) or Games-Howell (if unequal variances)",
    "For Success analyzed via logistic framework: use pairwise z-tests with adjusted standard errors or emmeans contrasts with appropriate link",
    "For Kruskal-Wallis robustness: Dunn's test with Bonferroni or Holm adjustment",
    "Focus contrasts on: Combined vs Sham, Combined vs single-modality conditions, ICMS Only vs Visual-only conditions, Bright vs Dim Visual Only"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control at alpha=0.05 across all tests within each response variable family; for Success as distinct family, apply separate FDR control; consider Bonferroni for family-wise error rate control if fewer than 50 comparisons per family; document all m-values for transparency",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Categorical-response prediction task: stimulation paradigm is unordered categorical with 5 levels. Recommend multinomial logistic regression with regularization (elastic net) using standardized performance variables as predictors. Alternative: random forest or gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM) with class weights to handle severe imbalance (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505, ratio ~14:1). Avoid ordinal logistic regression since paradigms lack natural ordering. Evaluate with stratified cross-validation, metrics: balanced accuracy, macro-averaged F1, confusion matrix inspection, and multinomial deviance. Permutation importance and SHAP values for interpretability.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: assumed via experimental design with replication=3; verify no repeated-measure structure within sessions if Mouse is random effect",
    "Success as binary violates OLS assumptions—confirmed use of generalized linear model",
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm (Combined dominates at 63.7% of data) affects predictive model reliability for minority classes",
    "Potential outliers: Time-to-Target max=201.393 (possible censoring or error), Path Efficiency max=29.817 (strong right skew)",
    "Check for multicollinearity among predictors (Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD may correlate)",
    "Consider random effects for Mouse (8 levels) to account for between-subject variation in ANOVA and mixed models"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: lowest Success (mean=0.273), highest Time-to-Target (mean=4.682), lowest Path Efficiency (mean=0.308), lowest Average Speed (mean=10.737), lowest AD (mean=0.236)",
    "Combined stimulation (ICMS + Visual cues) expected superior to either modality alone: highest Success (mean=0.780), fast Time-to-Target (mean=2.562), high Path Efficiency (mean=0.502), high Average Speed (mean=12.833), highest AD (mean=0.399)",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only intermediate performance, with ICMS Only potentially outperforming Dim Visual Only (Success: 0.685 vs 0.673; Time-to-Target: 3.053 vs 3.140)",
    "Bright Visual Only showing strong performance near Combined levels (Success: 0.785 vs 0.780) despite smaller sample, suggesting visual salience matters",
    "Statistical significance uncertain for Bright vs Combined and ICMS vs Dim due to effect size vs variance tradeoffs; post-hoc power depends on residual variance",
    "Predictive model likely to achieve high accuracy for Combined classification but struggle with Sham, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only discrimination due to sample imbalance"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Cross-sectional summary statistics mask trial-level variability and learning effects across replication 3",
    "Mouse as blocking factor not incorporated in summary; if mice cluster by performance, ANOVA assumptions violated without mixed-effects structure",
    "Time-to-Target extreme value (201.393s) may indicate timeout or data quality issue affecting variance estimates",
    "Success binary nature means ANOVA inappropriate without transformation or alternative methodology",
    "Severe class imbalance (n_Combined=48846, n_Sham=3505) limits inferential power for minority paradigms and predictive generalization",
    "AD interpretation as 'angular dispersion' assumes circular statistics validity; verify 0-1 boundedness matches expected domain",
    "No information on within-mouse trial counts or session structure prevents repeated-measures modeling",
    "Single temperature/model/prompt_template condition restricts external validity to broader parameter space"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept for each continuous response variable to account for clustering; use generalized linear mixed model (binomial) for Success. Then implement multinomial logistic regression with L2 regularization and class weights for paradigm prediction, evaluating with stratified 5-fold cross-validation. If prediction accuracy remains poor for minority classes, consider one-vs-rest binary classifiers or cost-sensitive learning. Visualize partial dependence to characterize decision boundaries across performance metrics."
}
